leads.name: Araucaria of Plaza de Calvo Sotelo
leads.reason: NEW this pass (2026-08-23), found via the Ayuntamiento de Alicante's own 'Paseos y arboles singulares en el Centro Tradicional de Alicante' walking-route brochure (stop 8, Plaza de Calvo Sotelo, ~90m from the existing Gabriel Miro cluster), which calls it 'una enorme araucaria' alongside a Platanus x hispanica and an Ulmus minor. Not in the Valencian regional register at all (checked: no Araucaria heterophylla/excelsa entry anywhere near Alicante city in data/registers/valencia-arboles-monumentales.json, nearest is >70km away), so there is no register source to pair with the brochure. The Spanish Wikipedia article 'Plaza de Calvo Sotelo' and the article 'Arboles singulares de Alicante' both mention it, but both cite the same Ayuntamiento brochure as their only source, and one further blog (anticalicante.blogspot.com) explicitly credits its text to Wikipedia. Two searches for an independent source (news coverage, a girth/height measurement, a photo with scale) found nothing beyond restatements of the same brochure. Held as a lead rather than shipped: one real source only, no measurements at all (no girth, height or age), so it fails both the two-source bar and the derived-age requirement. A street-level or satellite check for the tree's size, or any independent press mention, would unblock it. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-26, no change: fetched the Ayuntamiento's own 'Fichas: Arboles' species PDF directly (senderos-centro-arboles.pdf), which confirms the species page and photo caption 'Araucaria en Plaza Calvo Sotelo' but is the same brochure family, not an independent source, and carries no individual measurements. A further search for a girth/age figure returned nothing new. Still one source only; still unshippable.

leads.species: Ficus microcarpa / Ficus macrophylla / Grevillea robusta
leads.reason: A long row of individually registered figs (and two Grevillea robusta) strung along roughly 150-300m of a stretch this project's own data has referred to as 'Passeig de Canalejas continuing toward Portal de Elche' (a separate, more distant stretch, 0.4-0.75km from centre, from the small Portal de Elche plaza grove at 300/301/302/303 which sits right at the plaza itself, 0.1-0.15km from centre; the two should not be confused despite both carrying 'Canalejas' in nearby names). Reads as a continuous avenue rather than individual collectible points (see the ensemble rule); the one individually named, most distinctive specimen from this stretch (register_id 507, 'Ficus del Passeig de Canalejas') already shipped as ali_005. NOTE: register_ids 853 and 614, formerly listed here, are RESOLVED: 853 shipped as ali_011 (2026-08-15) with 614 explicitly folded into that same entry as one grove (see ali_011's verify_notes). Register_id 3095, formerly listed here, is also RESOLVED and removed from this group: it turned out not to be part of this avenue at all, but a standalone tree 1.2km further north in its own plaza (Plaza de la Pipa, Carolinas Bajas), shipped individually 2026-08-26 as ali_014. Exact street addresses and public/private status of the remaining stretch (toward Portal de Elche) were not individually confirmed within this pass's time budget.

Same station-forecourt trio as register_id 3096 (Avenida de Salamanca, beside Alacant Terminal's main facade; alicante.es and alicantepress both confirm 'tres ficus con jardinera' at this exact site as one of six citywide monumental-ficus panel locations). 3096 shipped 2026-08-17 as ali_010 (tallest/thickest of the three, 6.9m girth). 3097 (6.5m girth, 20m, 7m from 3096) and 3098 (6.7m girth, 20m, 58m from 3096) held as leads rather than shipped as separate entries, to avoid fragmenting one small forecourt grove into near-identical collectible points, matching the 300/302 precedent at Parque de Canalejas. Access note carried to ali_010: the immediately adjacent Plaza de la Estrella (Salamanca/Aguilera intersection) is, per an April 2026 todoalicante report, still a fenced-off construction site for the Parque Central project; the station-forecourt trees themselves are not inside it, but this should be re-checked if a future pass revisits.

A fourth 'Proteccion Generica' Ficus macrophylla (6.2m girth), but on Carrer de l'Esportista Ramon Mendizabal, ~0.9km from the Avenida de Salamanca station trio and not part of that cluster. More residential street; public/private status not individually confirmed within this pass's time budget.

leads.name: Ficus de la Finca La Concepció
leads.reason: CHECKED 2026-08-23: 7.7km from centre, girth 4.8m, height 15.4m, crown 29.5m (Generalitat Valenciana register, category Proteccion Generica). NOT in Alicante municipality: this is the Finca/Casa de la Concepcion in Sant Joan d'Alacant (Carrer Hernan Cortes, 8), a separate town on TRAM line 2, roughly 25 minutes end to end from Luceros plus a walk, so borderline for the day-trip boundary rather than clearly inside it. Turismo Sant Joan's own page (https://turismosantjoan.es/en/la-concepcion-estate/) independently confirms a ficus 'more than 100 years old' on the eastern edge of the property, 'included in the municipal catalog of protected trees', which is a genuine second source for species and a derived age (over a century) alongside the register. That is the good news. Access is the open question: the same page says 'the original perimeter fence has been removed' but 'a recent fence covered with heather surrounds this building', and current ownership plans to convert the historic house into a hostel; a separate search snippet (not independently verified by fetching the page itself) describes the grounds as having 'become a public park'. Those two claims are not flatly contradictory (garden open, building fenced) but this pass could not confirm which side of any fence the ficus stands on, and did not find a source stating opening hours or a free-access line in the terms this project needs for the access field. Hold as a lead: promising (named tree, two sources, real age derivation) but not yet clearable on hard rule 10's access test, and it belongs to a different town's future page as much as to Alicante's, which a later pass should decide with fresh eyes rather than this one guessing under a time box. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-26, no change: fetched a second Turismo Sant Joan page directly ('La Concepcion and Manzaneta Gardens'), which also does not state opening hours, an entry fee or a free-access line, only that 'the gardens have numerous centenary trees that today form part of the most beautiful public park in the municipality' (describing the wider Manzaneta grounds more than confirming which side of a fence this specific ficus sits on). Access still not clearable; do not ship without a source that states hours or an explicit open/closed line for this specific tree's spot.

leads.species: Ficus macrophylla / Phoenix dactylifera / Washingtonia robusta / Washingtonia filifera / Olea europaea
leads.reason: Not pursued this pass, per the brief's own steer toward the walkable named centre cluster over these: a scattered group of named-estate trees 8.0-9.5km from centre (Fincas Maxara, El Conde o La Pau, Santa Ana, L'Abril, Espinos, and unnamed others), all in Sant Joan d'Alacant/Mutxamel rather than Alicante itself. A quick check of 'Finca El Conde o La Pau' (register_id 1247's site) found a local heritage blog (anticalicante.blogspot.com) describing it as a ruin: 'irrigation no longer exists, the few remaining trees barely survive in the razed garden, and no one inhabits the house anymore', which reads as private and likely fails the access test outright. The others were not checked individually. Any future pass on these should expect private agricultural estates rather than public ground, and check access before spending time on names or ages.

blocked.reason: RE-CHECKED 2026-08-23, no change: fetched both todoalicante.es articles on the September 2025 elm collapse in Plaza Gabriel Miro directly (not just search snippets). Neither names a precise corner, adjacent building or which of the five registered elms fell; one only says the spot has no hostelry terraces nearby. Still no way to identify which four of the five register coordinates remain standing, so all five stay held rather than moved to leads: this is now a confirmed-unresolvable-by-search question, not just an unchecked one. A street-level photo or a follow-up city report naming the exact tree is the only thing that would unblock this.

CHECKED 2026-08-26: Carrer de l'Esportista Ramon Mendizabal 3, girth 6.2m, height 11m, crown 25m (Proteccion Generica). Cross-checked via OSM (node 13092900356, reg_ref=3099, denotation=natural_monument, protected=yes, figures match the register exactly) which sits inside the bbox of way 153247101, alt_name "Parque del Jardin Botanico" (a public park, San Fernando-Princesa Mercedes neighbourhood). The Spanish Wikipedia article "Parque El Botanico" independently confirms this exact tree (centenarian Ficus macrophylla, city-designated "a monumental tree of local interest") but states plainly: "su tronco se encuentra dentro de una parcela de una urbanizacion privada colindante, aunque la mitad de su copa se extiende hacia el parque" (the TRUNK stands on an adjacent private development parcel, Urbanizacion Gran Ficus, though half the canopy reaches into the public park). Per the hard limit "never deliver a tree ... on private land not genuinely open to visitors; when in doubt, leave it out", this is blocked rather than shipped: the trunk itself is not on public ground, only overhanging canopy is visible from the park side. It may be a legitimate view-only candidate under the wider project's viewing-place doctrine (visible from public park ground, pin marking the viewing spot rather than the trunk), which this verification pass is not positioned to apply; a session with full product context should decide rather than a verify pass guessing. Two sources agree on everything except access: the Valencia register (data/registers/valencia-arboles-monumentales.json, id 3099) and es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parque_El_Botanico.
